title: Cabin rental site with a range calendar, booked nights and seasonal pricing
prompt:
Build the website for Larchwood Cabins, three off-grid cabins in a quiet glen in the Cairngorms. Calm and outdoorsy: pine green, birch white and a warm rust accent, rounded cards, and a simple SVG illustration of each cabin (no photos). One index.html with hash routes #/ (home), #/cabin/fernbrook, #/cabin/heron, #/cabin/stag and #/trips. The header has the logo and the links Cabins and 'Trips (N)', where N counts saved bookings.

Cabins: Fernbrook Bothy (sleeps 2, dogs welcome, £95 a night, cleaning £40), Heron Lodge (sleeps 4, no dogs, £140 a night, cleaning £60) and Stag Barn (sleeps 8, dogs welcome, £260 a night, cleaning £90). Home shows a card for each with 'Sleeps N', 'From £X a night' and a 'Dog friendly' badge where it applies, linking to the cabin's page.

Cabin page: a short description, an availability calendar and a booking panel. The calendar shows two months side by side, weeks starting on Monday, beginning with October 2026; Previous and Next move one month at a time within October 2026 to January 2027. Ignore the real current date. Nights already booked (a night is named by the date it starts): Fernbrook 16 and 17 October; Heron 9, 10, 11, 23 and 24 October; Stag 31 October, 1 November and 24 to 26 December. Booked nights look struck through and cannot be a check-in day, but a booked night's date can be the check-out day.

Choosing dates: the first click sets check-in and the second sets check-out; a click on or before the check-in, or any click once both are set, starts again from that day. Highlight the range and show a line such as 'Tue 13 Oct → Fri 16 Oct · 3 nights'. A range containing a booked night shows 'Those dates include booked nights'. The minimum stay is 2 nights ('Minimum stay is 2 nights'), or 3 nights when any night falls from 20 December to 2 January ('Minimum stay over the festive period is 3 nights'). Invalid ranges cannot be reserved.

Pricing: each night costs the cabin rate, times 1.5 for festive nights (20 December to 2 January), plus £30 for Friday and Saturday nights. Stays of 7 nights or more get 10% off the nights. Add the cleaning fee, £25 per dog (0 to 2, only where dogs are welcome; Heron Lodge shows 'No dogs at Heron Lodge' instead of the dog control) and a visitor levy of £2 per adult per night. Guests: adults from 1 and children from 0, together at most the cabin's sleeps. The breakdown lists Nights, Long-stay discount (only when it applies, as a negative amount), Cleaning, Dogs (only with dogs), Visitor levy and Total, in pounds with two decimals and thousands separators.

Booking: name ('Please enter your name'), email ('Enter a valid email address') and a Reserve button. Success shows 'Booked! Your reference is LC-HL-1310' (LC, the cabin code FB, HL or SB, and the check-in day and month as DDMM) with the total. Bookings are saved in localStorage, block their nights in that cabin's calendar, and are listed on #/trips in check-in order with a Cancel button; with none it says 'No trips yet'.

At 390px wide the calendar shows one month at a time with Previous and Next, and the booking panel sits below it.

Guests: on Heron set 3 adults and try to add 2 children; on Stag press the dog plus button 3 times. title: Sunday league site with computed standings, tie-breakers and a score predictor
prompt:
Build the website of the Riverside Sunday League, an amateur football league, for its Division One season. Sporty and clean: grass green and chalk white with a navy accent, heavy headings and tabular numbers. Each club has a small SVG crest (a shield with its initials in its own colors). One index.html with hash routes #/table (the default), #/fixtures and #/team/<slug> (lowercase name with hyphens, e.g. #/team/elm-park-rangers); an unknown club shows 'Team not found'.

Results so far (home team first):
Round 1, Sun 6 Sep: Ashford Albion 2–0 Foundry Town; Brookside United 0–1 Elm Park Rangers; Canal Street 2–0 Dockyard Rovers.
Round 2, Sun 13 Sep: Elm Park Rangers 1–1 Ashford Albion; Dockyard Rovers 2–2 Foundry Town; Brookside United 2–0 Canal Street.
Round 3, Sun 20 Sep: Ashford Albion 0–1 Dockyard Rovers; Canal Street 2–4 Elm Park Rangers; Foundry Town 2–1 Brookside United.
Round 4, Sun 27 Sep: Canal Street 2–3 Ashford Albion; Brookside United 0–3 Dockyard Rovers; Elm Park Rangers 2–0 Foundry Town.
Round 5, Sun 4 Oct (not played yet): Ashford Albion v Brookside United; Foundry Town v Canal Street; Dockyard Rovers v Elm Park Rangers.

Table: computed from the results, with columns Pos, Club, P, W, D, L, GF, GA, GD (with a + sign when positive), Pts and Form. A win is worth 3 points and a draw 1. Rank by points, then goal difference, then goals scored, then the result of the match between the two clubs (if they have played), then alphabetically. Form shows the last three results as W, D or L pills, oldest on the left. Each row links to the club page.

Fixtures: the results grouped by round with their dates, and Round 5 as a predictor with two score boxes per fixture. A fixture counts as a prediction only when both boxes hold whole numbers from 0 to 20; an empty box just means no prediction, and any other entry shows 'Enter a whole number from 0 to 20' and is ignored. Counted predictions feed the table, form and club pages exactly like real results; the table then shows 'Includes N predicted results', a 'Clear predictions' button, and beside each club its movement compared with the table without predictions (▲1, ▼2 or –). Predictions persist in localStorage.

Club page: crest, name, position as an ordinal (e.g. '2nd'), P, W, D, L, GD and Pts, every match with its score and a W/D/L tag, and the next fixture.

At 390px the table shows only Pos, Club, P, GD and Pts, and the predictor fits the screen.

Predictor (find the Round 5 score inputs' selectors in the source; use type with a selector): scenario 1 in one call: on #/fixtures enter Ashford Albion 1–2 Brookside United, Foundry Town 2–2 Canal Street and Dockyard Rovers 3–0 Elm Park Rangers, go to #/table, screenshot and eval the rows. Scenario 2 on a fresh page (Clear predictions first if needed): enter only Ashford 2–2 Brookside and Dockyard 1–1 Elm Park, leave Foundry v Canal empty, check the table. Invalid: type -1, then 2.5, then 21 into one box with a valid number in the other box, press Tab and screenshot the message and the table. title: Recipe site with scaling, metric/US conversion and a merged shopping list
prompt:
Build Little Larder, a home-cooking recipe website with three recipes. Warm and friendly: a cream background, tomato red and herb green accents, rounded cards, and an SVG illustration of each dish (no photos). One index.html with hash routes #/ (recipes), #/recipe/<slug> (tomato-bean-soup, lemon-chicken-traybake, banana-oat-muffins) and #/list (shopping list).

Recipes (amount, ingredient, aisle):
Tomato & White Bean Soup, serves 4, 35 min, Vegetarian: 30 ml olive oil (Pantry), 1 onion (Produce), 3 garlic cloves (Produce), 800 g chopped tomatoes (Pantry), 480 g cannellini beans (Pantry), 750 ml vegetable stock (Pantry), 1 tsp smoked paprika (Pantry), 100 g baby spinach (Produce).
Lemon Herb Chicken Traybake, serves 4, 40 min: 900 g chicken thighs (Meat & fish), 700 g new potatoes (Produce), 1 lemon (Produce), 4 garlic cloves (Produce), 40 ml olive oil (Pantry), 2 tsp dried oregano (Pantry), 1 red onion (Produce), 150 g Greek yogurt (Dairy).
Banana Oat Muffins, makes 12, 50 min, Vegetarian: 3 ripe bananas (Produce), 150 g rolled oats (Pantry), 120 g plain flour (Pantry), 200 ml milk (Dairy), 2 eggs (Dairy), 50 ml honey (Pantry), 2 tsp baking powder (Pantry), 120 g Greek yogurt (Dairy).
Write 4 to 6 method steps for each.

Recipes page: cards with time and tags, chips 'Vegetarian' and 'Under 45 min', and a search box matching recipe names and ingredients. They combine; with no match show 'No recipes match'.

Recipe page: a servings stepper (1 to 12; the muffins go from 6 to 24 in steps of 6) that scales every amount, and a 'Start cooking' button that opens a step-by-step dialog with 'Step 1 of N', Back and Next buttons and ArrowLeft/ArrowRight; Escape closes it and returns focus to the button.

Units: a Metric / US switch in the header applies everywhere. Metric: grams and millilitres rounded to whole numbers. US: grams become ounces with one decimal (1 oz = 28.35 g); millilitres of 60 or more become cups rounded to the nearest quarter (1 cup = 240 ml; 'cup' up to 1, otherwise 'cups') and smaller amounts become tablespoons rounded to the nearest half (1 tbsp = 15 ml). In both systems tsp amounts and whole items are rounded to the nearest quarter and written with ¼, ½ and ¾, with the amount first (e.g. 1½ tsp smoked paprika, 4½ garlic cloves, 45 ml olive oil).

Shopping list: 'Add to list' adds a recipe at its current servings; adding it again replaces it. The list merges ingredients with the same name and unit across recipes, groups them under Produce, Meat & fish, Dairy and Pantry in that order, sorts them A–Z inside each group, and shows each recipe as a chip with a remove button. Each item has a checkbox that strikes it through. The header shows 'List (N)' with the number of list items. The list, the ticks and the unit choice persist in localStorage.

At 390px everything is one column and the cooking dialog fits the screen.
interaction_hints: Filters: click the Vegetarian chip, then Under 45 min, screenshot and eval the visible recipe titles; clear them, type yogurt in the search box (find its selector), then add Vegetarian; type xyz for the empty state. Scaling: on #/recipe/tomato-bean-soup press the servings plus button twice (4 → 6), screenshot the ingredient list, switch to US, screenshot again. On #/recipe/banana-oat-muffins press plus once (12 → 18), screenshot in Metric and US, and press minus until it stops (should stop at 6). Shopping list in one fresh call: soup at 6 → Add to list; traybake: press minus twice (4 → 2) → Add to list; muffins at 12 → Add to list; go to #/list, screenshot full_page, eval the header text; switch to US and screenshot; tick two items; reload and screenshot. Then go back to the soup, set 2 servings, Add to list again, check #/list (garlic cloves 3½), and remove the traybake chip. Cook mode: click Start cooking, press ArrowRight twice and screenshot, press ArrowLeft, press Escape and eval document.activeElement.textContent. Mobile: run interact with --width 390 --height 844 on #/, a recipe and #/list with full_page screenshots; open the cooking dialog there.

rubric.criterion: The recipes page shows the three recipes with SVG dish illustrations, times (35, 40 and 50 min), serves/makes and tags; each card opens its #/recipe/<slug> route, which also loads directly, and every recipe has 4 to 6 method steps.

Filters combine: Vegetarian + Under 45 min shows only Tomato & White Bean Soup; Under 45 min alone shows the soup and the traybake; searching yogurt shows the traybake and the muffins, and with Vegetarian only the muffins; xyz shows 'No recipes match'.

The soup scaled to 6 servings in Metric shows exactly 45 ml olive oil, 1½ onion, 4½ garlic cloves, 1200 g chopped tomatoes, 720 g cannellini beans, 1125 ml vegetable stock, 1½ tsp smoked paprika and 150 g baby spinach.

The soup at 6 servings in US shows 3 tbsp olive oil, 42.3 oz chopped tomatoes, 25.4 oz cannellini beans, 4¾ cups vegetable stock and 5.3 oz baby spinach, with 1½ tsp smoked paprika and 4½ garlic cloves unchanged.

The muffin stepper moves in steps of 6 between 6 and 24; at 18 it shows 4½ ripe bananas, 225 g rolled oats, 180 g plain flour, 300 ml milk, 3 eggs, 75 ml honey, 3 tsp baking powder and 180 g Greek yogurt, and in US 1¼ cups milk and ¼ cup honey.

With the soup at 6, the traybake at 2 and the muffins at 12, #/list shows 21 items as 'List (21)' under Produce, Meat & fish, Dairy, Pantry in that order, A–Z within each, with merged amounts 6½ garlic cloves, 65 ml olive oil and 195 g Greek yogurt, plus 450 g chicken thighs, ½ lemon, 1½ onion and ½ red onion as separate lines.
The same list in US shows ¼ cup olive oil, 6.9 oz Greek yogurt, 42.3 oz chopped tomatoes, ¾ cup milk and 3½ tbsp honey.
Adding the soup again at 2 servings replaces it (garlic cloves become 3½ and olive oil 35 ml), and removing the traybake chip leaves 16 items with 1½ garlic cloves.
After a reload the list (recipes, servings and merged amounts), the ticked items (still struck through) and the chosen unit system are all restored.
Start cooking opens a dialog showing 'Step 1 of N'; ArrowRight/Next and ArrowLeft/Back move between steps, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the Start cooking button.

title: Fell-walking guide with Naismith times, unit switching and an elevation profile
prompt:
Build Fellwise, a guide to eight Lake District fell walks. Outdoorsy and map-like: slate blue, bracken orange and moss green on a pale paper background, contour-line decoration in SVG, and clear data typography. One index.html with hash routes #/ (walks), #/walk/<slug> (lowercase name, apostrophes removed, spaces as hyphens, e.g. #/walk/blencathra-by-halls-fell) and #/logbook.

Walks (name, grade, distance, elevations in metres at 0 km, 1 km, 2 km and so on, then at the finish):
Catbells Ridge, Moderate, 5.6 km: 90, 215, 451, 330, 180, 110, 90.
Tarn Hows Circuit, Easy, 3.2 km: 190, 215, 205, 232, 190.
Helvellyn via Striding Edge, Hard, 12.4 km: 150, 380, 620, 860, 950, 850, 700, 520, 400, 290, 200, 160, 150, 150.
Buttermere Shore, Easy, 7.2 km: 115, 120, 118, 130, 125, 122, 119, 121, 115.
Scafell Pike from Wasdale, Hard, 9.0 km: 80, 350, 620, 890, 978, 700, 420, 200, 90, 80.
Loughrigg Fell, Moderate, 6.8 km: 60, 180, 290, 335, 210, 150, 90, 60.
Ullswater Way, Easy, 11.0 km: 150, 175, 160, 190, 230, 200, 185, 210, 175, 160, 170, 150.
Blencathra by Hall's Fell, Hard, 7.4 km: 230, 520, 868, 640, 450, 330, 270, 240, 230.

Numbers: ascent is the sum of every rise between consecutive points. Estimated time uses Naismith's rule: distance divided by the walking speed plus one hour per 600 m of ascent, rounded up to the next 15 minutes and shown like '2 h 15 min' or '3 h 00 min' ('45 min' under an hour). The header has a Pace setting (Relaxed 4 km/h, Steady 5 km/h, Brisk 6 km/h; default Steady) and a Units switch (Metric, Imperial). Imperial shows miles with one decimal (1 km = 0.621371 mi) and feet rounded to the nearest 10 (1 m = 3.28084 ft) with thousands separators. Both settings persist in localStorage.

Walks page: a card per walk with grade, distance, ascent and time; grade chips (Easy, Moderate, Hard; several at once, none means all), a sort select (Quickest first with ties going to the shorter walk, Shortest first, Least ascent, Name A–Z), and 'Showing N of 8 walks'.

Walk page: distance, ascent, 'High point <n> m' and time, and an SVG elevation profile drawn from the points. Hovering the profile, or focusing it and pressing ArrowLeft/ArrowRight, moves a marker from point to point and shows a readout like '3.0 km · 330 m' (in Imperial '1.9 mi · 1,080 ft'). A 'Mark as walked' toggle adds the walk to the logbook.

From top to bottom on desktop: a dark announcement bar; a white header with a round logo, the Halden AUDIO wordmark, five links with Headphones underlined in copper, a pill search field and account and bag icons; a breadcrumb; the product hero with four thumbnails beside a large warm stage showing the headphones with its pills and buttons, and the buy box (serif name, rating, price with the old price struck through, payment line, colour swatches, a delivery / pick-up selector, stock line, Add to cart with a wishlist button and trust badges); four feature tiles; a Technical specifications card beside a Compare the H-series table with the H7 column tinted; Customer reviews with a summary card (average, star histogram, feature meters) next to filter chips and three review cards; four accessory cards; a dark help card beside a five-question FAQ with the first question open; and a dark footer. On mobile the header keeps the logo, search, bag and menu icons; dots under the stage replace the thumbnails; everything stacks in one column; the feature tiles and accessories form 2x2 grids; the comparison drops the H5 column; the review sort and colour notes are hidden; and the footer links sit in three columns. The product name, section headings and big numbers use Liberation Serif and everything else uses Lato. Draw the headphones, logo, icons, stars, check marks and accessories with inline SVG. Match the layout, sizes, spacing, colors, typography and every piece of text as closely as you can in both layouts.

rubric.criterion: Desktop structure matches desktop.png: announcement bar, header, breadcrumb, a hero with an 88px thumbnail column and a 560px stage on the left and the buy box on the right, 'Built for long listening' with four tiles in one row, two equal cards (specifications | comparison), reviews with a narrow summary card left of the chips and three stacked review cards, four accessory cards in a row, a dark help card beside the FAQ list, and a dark four-column footer, on a centered column about 1184px wide at roughly the same vertical positions and total page height.

Mobile structure matches mobile.png at 390px: the announcement keeps only 'Free 2-day shipping on orders over $99'; the header shows only the logo, a search icon, the bag with 2 and a menu icon; the stage is full width with four dots (the first elongated) and no thumbnails; the buy box follows with its three trust badges stacked; the feature tiles are a 2x2 grid with the icon above the value; the cards and review summary stack; the comparison shows only H7 and H9 Studio; review cards put the stars and date on one line above the title with no colour note; accessories are 2x2; the help card sits above the FAQ; the footer links are in three columns; nothing overflows horizontally.

The header and gallery match: the round dark logo with copper ear cups, 'Halden' in serif with spaced 'AUDIO', links Headphones (copper underline), Earbuds, Speakers, Accessories and Journal, 'Search products', a bag badge '2'; the breadcrumb Home / Headphones / Over-ear / Halden H7 Wireless; thumbnails of the graphite headphones (outlined), a close-up of the round cup, a sand pair and a cobalt pair; and a stage drawing of graphite headphones seen from the front (arched headband with a stitched inner cushion, silver sliders and yokes, two cups seen edge-on with copper trim, a soft floor shadow) with the 'New colour: Cobalt' pill, a zoom button, the dark '360° view' pill and '1 / 4'.

The buy box matches: copper 'OVER-EAR · WIRELESS', 'Halden H7 Wireless', 'Adaptive noise-cancelling headphones with a 60-hour battery', 4.6 stars with '1,284 reviews' and '86 answered questions', '$279.00' with '$349.00' struck through and 'Save $70', 'or 4 interest-free payments of $69.75 · Learn more', 'Colour: Graphite' and '4 colours' over graphite (ringed), sand, moss and cobalt swatches, the selected 'Free delivery' row (Arrives Thu, Oct 1 – Fri, Oct 2, Free) and 'Pick up at Halden SoHo' (Ready in 2 hours · 3 left in stock, Free), 'In stock and ready to ship', a dark 'Add to cart · $279.00' button with a round heart button, and '2-year warranty', '45-day free returns' and 'Recycled packaging'.

The tiles read 60 h 'Battery with ANC on', 8 mics 'Adaptive noise cancelling', 254 g 'Featherweight frame' and LDAC 'Hi-Res wireless audio' with copper icon squares and gray detail lines, and the specifications card ('Model H7-W · Firmware 3.2', 'Spec sheet (PDF)') lists exactly Driver, Frequency response 4 Hz – 40 kHz, Impedance 32 Ω, Battery life 60 h with ANC · 80 h without, Charging, Bluetooth 5.4 multipoint (2 devices), Codecs SBC, AAC, aptX Adaptive, LDAC, Microphones 8, Weight 254 g and In the box, with gray labels and bold values.

The comparison table matches: columns H5 $179, H7 $279 under a copper 'THIS MODEL' tag in a tinted rounded column, and H9 Studio $449; rows Battery life 40 h / 60 h / 50 h, Noise cancelling Standard / Adaptive / Adaptive Pro, Spatial audio, LDAC Hi-Res and Wear detection with a dash for H5 and green checks otherwise, Multipoint checked for all three, Weight 238 g / 254 g / 312 g and Case Soft pouch / Hard case / Hard case, plus 'Compare all' in the card header.

The review summary matches: a large serif 4.6 with partial stars and 'Based on 1,284 reviews', amber histogram bars for 5 to 1 stars with counts 960, 214, 58, 27 and 25 and lengths in that proportion, 'RATED BY FEATURE' meters in a 2x2 grid (Comfort 4.7, Sound quality 4.8, Battery life 4.9, Noise cancelling 4.5) drawn as five dark segments, and '94% of reviewers recommend the H7' in a gray box.

The review list matches: 'Show all 1,284 reviews' and an outlined 'Write a review' in the header, chips 'All reviews' (dark), '5 stars (960)', 'Verified only' and 'Mentions comfort' with 'Sort: Most helpful', and three cards: 'Quiet flights, finally' (5 stars, Sep 14, 2026, Priya S., Graphite, Helpful (48)), 'Great sound, the app needs work' (4 stars, Sep 2, 2026, Marcus T., Sand, Helpful (21)) and 'Battery that lasts all week' (5 stars, Aug 27, 2026, Elin K., Moss, Helpful (17)), each with a colored initials avatar and a green 'Verified buyer' badge.

The lower sections match: accessory cards with SVG drawings of a hard case, a braided cable, two ear cushions and a stand, priced H-Series Hard Case $39.00, USB-C to 3.5 mm Cable $19.00, Memory-Foam Ear Cushions $29.00 and Aluminium Headphone Stand $59.00 with outlined Add pills that have a plus icon; the dark 'Questions, answered' card with a beige 'Chat with an expert' button and 'Mon–Sat, 9 am – 7 pm ET'; five FAQ rows with round plus buttons, the first open with a dark minus and its answer; and the footer with SHOP, SUPPORT and COMPANY columns, the 'Email address' / 'Subscribe' field and '© 2026 Halden Audio AS. All rights reserved.'

Typography and color match: Liberation Serif bold for the product name, section and card headings and big numbers, Lato elsewhere with a 900-weight price; a warm #faf8f5 page, near-black #1d1f22 text and buttons, copper #b8703f accents with pale copper #f6e3d3 fills, green #2f7d4f stock and checks, amber #e0a526 stars, and white cards with thin warm #e8e3dc borders and about 18px radii.

Everything is real HTML text (the specifications and comparison are real table markup) with inline SVG or CSS for the logo, headphones, icons, stars, checks and accessories and no raster images, and both layouts come from one index.html via media queries.

title: Recreate a poster-style music festival page with a stage timetable
prompt: Recreate the attached home page of Tidelines Festival 2026, a three-day coastal festival at Saltmarsh Park, North Bay, as a real HTML/CSS page at 1280px wide. Bold and poster-like: warm sand with navy, coral, teal, amber and violet accents. From top to bottom: a header with a round sun-and-waves logo mark, the TIDELINES wordmark with a small coral 2026, six nav links with Lineup underlined, a monospace date and a coral Buy tickets pill; a rounded navy hero with a pill, the huge heavy headline TIDELINES over FESTIVAL 2026, dates and place, two pill buttons, and on the right a layered sunset illustration (a striped sun, birds, a lighthouse, two dunes, three rows of waves, a round coral badge and a white chip); The lineup as three day cards (Saturday in navy), each with two large uppercase headliners, a bold tier of four names, a lighter tier of six and a more-artists line; the Saturday timetable: day tabs and a grid of four stage columns against an hourly axis from 14:00 to 01:00, where every set is a tinted block positioned and sized by its start and end time and the two headliners are solid blocks; Find your way, an illustrated site map (lagoon, sea, pier, camping, paths, ten numbered markers, a compass and a scale bar) with a legend, beside three info cards; four ticket cards (a sold-out Early Bird, a navy Best value Weekend Pass, Weekend + Camping and Day Ticket); a four-question FAQ; and a navy footer with link columns and a newsletter field. Type is Inter in heavy weights, with DejaVu Sans Mono for eyebrows, times and small labels. Draw the logo, illustration, map and icons with inline SVG. Match the layout, sizes, spacing, colors, typography and every piece of text as closely as you can.

rubric.criterion: The layout matches the target: header, a 420px rounded navy hero with the illustration filling its right half, three equal lineup cards, a full-width timetable card, a Find your way row (wide map card on the left, three stacked info cards on the right), four equal ticket cards, the FAQ (heading column plus a 2x2 grid) and a full-width navy footer, all on a centered column about 1152px wide at roughly the same vertical positions and total page height (about 3,400px).

The header and hero text match: the round logo mark, 'TIDELINES' with a small coral '2026', links Lineup (coral underline), Timetable, Map, Tickets, Info and FAQ, '17–19 JUL · NORTH BAY' in monospace and a coral 'Buy tickets' pill; in the hero the pill '3 DAYS · 4 STAGES · 62 ARTISTS', a huge sand-colored 'TIDELINES', a letter-spaced coral 'FESTIVAL 2026', '17–19 July' over 'FRI – SUN' and 'Saltmarsh Park' over 'NORTH BAY COAST' separated by a vertical rule, a coral 'Buy tickets' and an outlined 'See the lineup' button.

The hero illustration matches: a navy-to-plum-to-orange sunset sky with small stars, a large amber sun cut by four horizontal stripes that thicken downward, three small navy birds, a coral-and-white striped lighthouse on the dunes, two sand dunes, three rows of scalloped teal waves getting darker toward the bottom, a round coral badge 'NEW IN 2026 / THE PIER / STAGE' with a dashed inner ring at the top right, and a white chip 'Sat 18 · Solenne closes the Main Stage' with a coral dot.

The lineup matches: the eyebrow 01 · WHO'S PLAYING, 'The lineup' and the right-aligned 'Sixty-two artists, three days, four stages by the water.'; cards FRIDAY 17 JULY (teal rule), SATURDAY 18 JULY (navy card, coral rule) and SUNDAY 19 JULY (amber rule) with the headliners MARLOW BAY / THE KESTRELS, SOLENNE / GLASS ATLAS and ORCA SUMMER / DELPHINE, three coral stars, the bold four-name tier and gray six-name tier on two lines each exactly as in the target (e.g. 'Rook & Wren · Midnight Ferry' / 'Tamsin Lowe · Night Swim' with coral dots), and '+ 8 MORE ARTISTS', '+ 9 MORE ARTISTS', '+ 9 MORE ARTISTS'.

The timetable frame matches: the eyebrow 02 · WHEN AND WHERE, 'Saturday timetable', 'Gates open 12:00 · last music 01:00' and tabs Fri 17, Sat 18 (dark, selected) and Sun 19; a card with stage headers Main Stage 'big nights' (coral square), Lagoon 'indie & folk' (teal), Dune Tent 'electronic' (amber) and The Pier 'DJs till late' (violet), monospace hour labels 14:00 to 01:00 on evenly spaced dashed lines, vertical column rules, and the footnote 'All times BST. Set times can change: check the Tidelines app on the day.' with a Set / Headliner legend.

All 19 sets sit in the right column at the right height and length for their times: Main Stage Bex Arno 14:00–15:00, Coastline Choir 15:45–16:45, Tamsin Lowe 17:30–18:30, Rook & Wren 19:15–20:30 and SOLENNE 21:30–23:00; Lagoon Fenn 14:30–15:30, Kaia Moon 16:15–17:15, Lio Sandoval 18:00–19:00, Midnight Ferry 19:45–21:00 and GLASS ATLAS 22:15–23:45; Dune Tent The Driftwoods 15:00–16:00, Harbor Static 16:45–17:45, Wavelength Duo 18:30–19:30, Night Swim 20:15–21:45 and Kite Theory 23:15–01:00; The Pier Tern Club 14:00–16:00, Low Orbit 16:30–18:30, Moss Parade 19:00–21:00 and Low Tide Sound System 21:30–00:30. Regular sets are pale tints with a left border in the stage color; SOLENNE (solid coral) and GLASS ATLAS (solid teal) have large white names and a HEADLINER tag.

The Find your way row matches: the eyebrow 03 · PLAN YOUR WEEKEND, 'Find your way', 'Between the lagoon and the sea, ten minutes from North Bay.'; a sand map with a pale-teal lagoon labeled THE LAGOON, the sea along the bottom labeled NORTH BAY, a wooden pier, a green CAMPING area with eight teal tents, round green trees, white dashed paths, markers 1 (coral), 2 (teal), 3 (amber), 4 (violet) and 5–10 (navy), a north compass and a '0 / 200 m' scale bar; a legend in two rows of five (1 Main Stage, 2 Lagoon, 3 Dune Tent, 4 The Pier, 5 Food court, 6 Campsites, 7 Main gate, 8 Shuttle stop, 9 First aid, 10 Water refill); and the cards Getting here ('SHUTTLES 11:00–02:00'), Camping ('OPENS THU 16 JULY 16:00') and Accessibility ('ACCESS@TIDELINES.FM') with coral, teal and violet icon tiles and their sentences.

Typography and color match: Inter with 900-weight headlines, headliners and prices, DejaVu Sans Mono for eyebrows, dates, hour labels, set times and ticket names; a sand #f7f0e3 page, navy #13294b hero and featured cards, coral #ef5a3c, teal #1a9b8e, amber #f2a93b and violet #6d5bd0 accents, cream #fffaf1 cards with 1px #e3d7c2 borders and about 22px radii, and fully rounded pills and buttons.

The tickets match: the eyebrow 04 · GET IN, 'Tickets' and 'Prices include booking fees. Under-12s go free with a paying adult.'; a grayed EARLY BIRD card with £169 struck through, a SOLD OUT badge, 'Weekend · released in October' and a disabled 'Sold out' button; a navy WEEKEND PASS card £189 with a coral BEST VALUE badge, 'Fri–Sun · per person', amber checks and a coral 'Buy weekend pass'; WEEKEND + CAMPING £249 'Thu–Mon · per person' with 'Buy with camping'; DAY TICKET £79 'Friday, Saturday or Sunday' with 'Choose a day'; each card lists its three checked features (e.g. 'Re-entry until 22:00 daily', 'Four nights by the dunes', 'Upgrade on site').

The FAQ and footer match: the eyebrow 05 · GOOD TO KNOW with 'Questions, answered' left of a 2x2 grid under dark rules (Can I leave and come back in?, Is the festival cashless?, What can I bring in?, Are children welcome?) with their answers; a navy footer with the logo and 'Three days of music, sea swims and long evenings on the North Bay coast.', amber monospace headings FESTIVAL, HELP, COMPANY and NEWSLETTER with four links each, a 'you@example.com' field joined to a coral 'Sign up', '© 2026 Tidelines Festival Ltd · Saltmarsh Park, North Bay' and 'Privacy · Terms · Cookies'.

Everything is real HTML text (lineup, set blocks, legend, tickets) with inline SVG or CSS for the logo, the hero illustration, the map, the icons and the check marks; there are no raster images, embedded screenshots or external resources.
